project_comments.note: Architectural gap: ApplicationTestCase::tearDown() does not reset the $_REQUEST superglobal between tests. Any test subclass that writes to $_REQUEST must maintain its own unset list in tearDown() or risk inter-test pollution. This was the root cause of the WP-002 failure (RecordTieInTest) and is a recurring hazard — especially for tie-in tests whose base classes cache results derived from $_REQUEST. Recommended fix in a future WP: add a $_REQUEST backup/restore mechanism to ApplicationTestCase (similar to PHPUnit's backupGlobals, but scoped to the keys the base class knows about) or document the pattern in testing.md as a required convention for any test that writes to superglobals.

Synthesis observation: The most actionable follow-up from this session is adding $_REQUEST backup/restore to ApplicationTestCase::tearDown(). The WP-002 failure (RecordTieInTest inter-test pollution) and the Reviewer's independent architectural note both converge on the same root cause. The per-class tearDown() workaround in RecordTieInTest is correct but creates a recurring obligation: every future test class that writes to superglobals must replicate this pattern. A single base-class fix eliminates the class of failure entirely. This should be the first WP in the next cleanup plan.
